To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Lactobacillaceae is a monophyletic group that contains four subgeneric clusters that are not monophyletic and that the genus Lactococcus is a sister genus to the Lactobacilli.

(i) a single, congruent phylogrouping of the genus Lactococcus could not be identified; (ii) the genus is composed of four subgroups; (iii) a group-specific gene cluster possibly involved purine metabolism was identified; and (iv) a single-gene phylogeny of the genus L. plantarum is more robust than that of the 16S gene.

Lactobacilli can be divided into four subgeneric groups, that these groups are functionally distinguishable by their absent genes, and that the genus is likely to be subdivided into novel genera in the future.
